Meridian GRC mockup - HTML edition (R9 2026-08-23)

The full demo as 43 files, every one an .html under 1 MB, so each file crosses the firewall on its own. The files run exactly as they are - no renaming, no conversion, no unpacking tool. All but index.html are the app’s JS carried with an .html name; Edge runs a <script src> target by its content, not its extension.

Set up once

  1. Make a folder, e.g. C:\GRC\demo-html\ (Documents works if C:\ is locked down), with three subfolders: kernel, modules, data.
  2. Place every file per the packing list below. index.html and this file sit at the root.
  3. Double-click index.html. Click Preflight in the banner: it must say NO TRAPPED ERRORS with every entity loaded (850 RAUs, 8,000 MCRs, 5,146 controls…).

If Edge refuses to open a file that came from outside, clear the download mark first: right-click the file → Properties → tick Unblock → OK. Files you create locally never have it.

Changed in this build - carry these across

Nothing to carry. Every app file in this build is byte-identical to the previous committed build. (This READ-ME regenerates every build; bring it across when convenient.)

Updating one file at a time

  • Replace the one changed .html in its folder, then hard-refresh the open demo (Ctrl+F5). That is the whole update. Confirm in Preflight: the module version table and release badge show what is actually loaded.
  • The kit and runbook name files the canonical way - modules/rcsa.js here is modules\rcsa.html. Same content, same Copilot workflow; just save with the .html name.
  • A brand-new module still needs its one <script> line added in index.html, same as the .js edition.
  • Large data entities ship split as -part1..N; every part must be present, in the order index.html lists. Data you rebuild locally (e.g. from DataForge) has no transfer limit - one whole-entity file saved as .html can replace all its part lines with a single line.
  • index.html normally sits at the structure root. To run it from somewhere else, open it in Notepad and follow the <base href> comment near the top: point it at the folder that holds kernel\ modules\ data\.
